What are cookies?

Cookies are small data files that are placed on your computer or mobile device when you visit a website. Cookies are widely used by website owners in order to make their websites work, or to work more efficiently, as well as to provide reporting information.

Cookies set by the website owner (in this case, Kush Valley Collective) are called "first party cookies". Cookies set by parties other than the website owner are called "third party cookies". extractPost[\"buying-originals-weed-at-o.body:
The second official retailer of Originals has just opened at 6220 Federal Blvd in sunny San Diego this past Cinco de Mayo. Those in search of award-winning genetics and the most cutting-edge cannabis products will find our new dispensary a welcoming home. Alongside our own popular flower products, you’ll find the same brands and innovators we carry at Originals Factory & Weed Shop in LA.

Originals is a family-owned business of LA natives that’s been serving the Los Angeles community high-quality cannabis since 2006. Quality control is our biggest concern, and it shows from the menu we curate to the flower we cultivate. The relationships we’ve built over the past decade and a half come to life on our lavish menu. Many of the celebrities working in cannabis have become our friends over the years and keep us in good supply.

Open seven days a week from 10 am-9 pm, and closing at 8 on Sundays, we cater to the community with accessibility. Customers can feel at home in our spacious and sleek new showroom that features numerous display cases of California’s best weed products. Ask a budtender about what the freshest flower or most popular edibles are and trust that you’re in good hands. Consider ordering online through our Weedmaps page in order to skip the line.

The Freshest Flower In SD

At Originals San Diego, you’ll find an artisanal curation of California’s premium products alongside our name brands. We’re keeping the freshest cuts of our in-house strains grown indoors at our Originals Weed Factory & Weed Shop in LA. You can purchase our premium cannabis flower in eighths. More cost-conscious customers can now also find our Originals Small Buds representing all of our same sought-after strains at a more affordable price. Current Small Buds strains include Wedding Cake, Oakstradam OG, London Pound Cake, Originals OG, and Divorce Cake x Zkittlez Cake.

Premium Eighths

The following strains are available in premium eighths from Originals: Gelato, Animal Face, Oakstradam OG, Wedding Cake, and Originals OG. Read more below about each of these strains and understand where we get our name. These are the original cuts of some of the most popular indica strains on the West Coast.

Gelato

Originals’ Gelato is true to the legend this hybrid strain has built. A cross between Sunset Sherbet and Thin Mint GSC, this strain has risen into infamy for its potentially euphoric highs and heavily sedative effects. As the name suggests, this strain reeks of dessert-like aromas that come across sweet, fruity, and spicy. Rich purple and green hues decorate the nugs with fiery orange pistils interwoven that offer illuminating contrast. The resinous layer of trichomes coating its surface shimmer like crystals. A THC powerhouse, Gelato has become a favorite among creatives that claim it may provide a strong physical high. Medical users might find the Gelato strain to be ideal for combating insomnia, fatigue, and chronic pain.

Animal Face

The Animal Face strain by Originals is a rare sativa-dominant OG Kush variety that takes on more of a piney and gassy terpene profile with cookie undertones. By crossing Face-Off OG with Animal Mints, you end up with this energizing hitter. This strain comes from the geniuses at Seed Junky Genetics. It is known for producing potentially body-numbing and mood-lifting highs. The nugs are dense with light and dark green coloration, showing off a glittering coating of trichomes on its surface. Drawing from famous Californian genetics, this strain may hit hard like an OG at first, but leave you functional enough to still get things done. Our Animal Face strain might also be useful for anyone dealing with inflammation, nausea, or mental and physical stress.

Oakstradam OG

Originals’ Oakstradam OG strain is a celebrity cut of OG Kush developed by Oaksterdam University in Oakland. The origins of this strain are said to be from crossing a NorCal strain with a Hindu Kush plant from Amsterdam. This heavy indica exhibits all of the classic characteristics of a potent OG taken to the extreme. Wildly dense buds show off deep green hues with dark red pistils. A thick blanket of resinous trichomes covers its surface, holding the nugs together like glue. Originals’ Oakstradam OG is known for its loud peppery, sweet, and musky flavors that might promote stress relief and create a sense of stoney euphoria.

Wedding Cake

The Originals Wedding Cake strain may turn any day into a special occasion. A potent indica-hybrid strain from Seed Junky Genetics, this beauty comes from crossing Triangle Kush with Animal Mints. Pale and dark green with ripe orange pistils, each nug has a frosty layer of trichomes. On the nose, you’ll notice tart vanilla aromas with hoppy undertones. If the terps don’t get you, the high THC content of our Wedding Cake strain is sure to leave a lasting impression. Smoking some of our Wedding Cake may uplift your mind and put your body at ease. This strain might be a welcoming companion to anyone suffering from depression, anxiety, or stress.

Originals OG

The Mac Daddy of OG Kush varieties, the Originals OG is some serious kush. You’ll notice an incredibly sweet lemon aroma on the nose. As well as its brilliant green foliage that has curly orange pistils poking out. Dense to the touch, the Originals OG has a short, yet pointy appearance that dully glimmers from the yellowed trichomes that wrap its surface. Those looking for the iconic calm that OG’s may provide will delight in this strain. The sweetness from the aroma still comes out amidst a mildly spicy smoke. Medical may find this strain to be a consistent cut of OG for anxiety relief.

Cannabis books are sweeping the nation. The legalization of cannabis is causing the cannabis industry to explode with new ideas. Many people that once thought of cannabis as a terrible, addictive drug are now joining the cannabis community. The growth of the industry is piquing many people’s curiosity about this amazing plant.

With this curiosity comes a plethora of information. A quick internet search and you’ll be inundated with cannabis books and resources. Here’s our list of favorite cannabis books for handy reference for any cannabis connoisseur.

Cannabis Books You’ll Love

1. Great: A Field Guide to Marijuana

extractPost[\"cannabis-legal-states-and-.seoTitle: Cannabis Legal States And Economic Growth
extractPost[\"cannabis-legal-states-and-.body:
In the last decade, several states have legalized cannabis for medical and recreational use. Following the last election, all but two states have some form of medical cannabis, while 15 have also allowed it for recreational use too. While regulations vary greatly from state to state, cannabis legal states have seen some significant economic benefits. Let’s take a closer look.

Legal Cannabis

What constitutes legal cannabis depends on the state. A majority of states in the US have legalized the plant for medical purposes. In other words, you need to have a doctor’s recommendation to enter a dispensary and buy cannabis. Every state has its own laws. For instance, legal medical cannabis products can’t have more than 5% THC. In medical-only states, you cannot purchase any cannabis products for recreational purposes.

In states that allow both medical and recreational cannabis, you still need a doctor’s recommendation to go into a medical dispensary. Adults 21 and older can enter a recreational dispensary to buy cannabis. Again, these states have several laws that state how much you can buy, how much you can grow, and where you can (and can’t) use your products.

Economic Effects Realized By Cannabis Legal States

Legalizing cannabis has had some significant economic effects on states throughout the country. In particular, these states have seen their economies grow. Let’s take a look at some of the benefits legal cannabis has provided:

Bringing in New Residents

One thing that legalizing cannabis has done is encourage new residents. When cannabis was legal in only a handful of states, many people moved to where they could get what they needed to manage various health conditions. Even today, people are deciding to move where they can get the products they want or need. New residents mean that more people are spending money in a given state.

Creating Jobs

Legalizing cannabis opens up numerous job opportunities. Dispensaries need owners and budtenders. States need qualified people to grow cannabis, transport it, transform it into a variety of products, and more. Opening up new jobs means that more people can work. As they earn money, they’ll put it back into the economy.

Additional Tax Revenue

If you’ve ever purchased recreational cannabis before, you’ve no doubt noticed that it comes with some pretty hefty taxes. The exact taxes vary between states, with many charging some combination of sales, excise, and cultivation tax.

Every state also determines how they want to use the taxes they generate via cannabis sales. For instance, California uses 60% of the revenue to support youth drug prevention and treatment programs. The other 40% is evenly split between environmental protection programs and the reduction of health and safety concerns. In Maine, the money goes into a general fund that the state uses to support educational services and train law enforcement teams.

Will Cannabis Ever Become Legal at the Federal Level?

Even though more and more states are legalizing cannabis, it remains illegal on the federal level. There have been several efforts to change this, but it hasn’t happened yet. Several lawmakers support full federal legalization, but there’s enough opposition still that it may not happen for a while. Only time will tell. What we do know is that legalizing cannabis can have some significant impacts on economic growth.

extractPost[\"thc-extract-for-fast-relie.body:
The cannabis market is full of all kinds of products, including flowers, edibles, tinctures, topicals, and more. There’s also a broad category of products called extracts. They can be full-spectrum extracts, or they can be isolates like THC extract. These products are becoming increasingly more popular as users discover their potency and versatility.

What’s THC Extract?

An extract is a specific type of cannabis concentrate that requires the use of a solvent such as ethanol, butane, or CO2. These solvents pull beneficial cannabinoids and terpenes from physical plant material. The exact processes used to create them vary based on the specific solvent. The resulting products, however, are all substantially more potent than the original plant.

Many extracts are full-spectrum, meaning they contain all of the cannabinoids and terpenes of the original plant. A THC extract, however, is a type of isolate. The process creates a product that only contains concentrated THC.

Types of THC Extracts

There are several different types of THC extracts on the market. Many of them get their names from their texture, while others get their names from the extraction process used to make them. Common types of THC extract include:

  • Shatter – a brittle, translucent extract that breaks apart easily
  • Crumble – a dry, crumbly extract
  • Budder – a smooth, creamy extract
  • Live resin – an extract created using fresh plants as opposed to dried and cured ones
  • Butane hash oil (BHO) – an extract made using butane
  • CO2 oil – an extract made using CO2 as the solvent

Ways to Use THC Extracts

The great thing about THC extracts is that they’re highly versatile. You can use them in a variety of different ways:

Dab Rig

One of the most common ways to use THC extracts is with a dab rig. You apply a small amount of your preferred extract onto the heated nail of the rig and inhale the smoke for fast, effective results.

Vaping

Using a vape pen, you can vape liquid extracts such as CO2 oil and BHO. You can also use what’s called a dab pen for other extracts. While both pen styles are similar, there is one significant difference. Vape pens use cartridges, which are filled with liquid extracts. Dab pens have a chamber into which you can place a bit of your preferred extract.

Adding a Bit to a Joint or Bowl

Adding a small amount of an extract to your joint or the bowl of your cannabis pipe provides some extra potency to your hits. It’s a great way to introduce yourself to just how strong extracts can be.

Mixing into Edibles

Another way to use extracts is to mix a small amount into your favorite recipes, creating potent edibles. One thing to keep in mind with this method of use is that edibles don’t provide the same fast-acting relief. Because you have to digest them first, it can take a bit longer to feel the effects.

Try THC Extract for Fast, Effective Relief

THC extracts provide fast-acting relief from a variety of symptoms. Not only are they effective, but you only need a small amount to achieve the desired results. Start low and gradually increase your dose until you find what works best for you.
